tip.title: End your shower with 30 seconds of cold
tip.why: In a Dutch trial of 3,018 adults, people who finished their daily shower with 30, 60 or 90 seconds of cold water for a month took 29% fewer sick days over the following three months than those who showered warm. The length of the cold burst didn't matter, and two-thirds of the cold group kept doing it on their own after the study ended. The benefit was fewer days off, not fewer illnesses: people felt better able to carry on.
how: Shower as usual, then turn the water as cold as it goes for the last 30 seconds.
Breathe out slowly through the gasp; it fades after about ten seconds.
Keep it to 30 seconds for the first week, then stretch to a minute if you like it.
tip.ask: Which shower today, morning or after the gym, is the easy one to end cold?

markets.headline: Stocks rebounded on Wednesday as CoreWeave's beat revived the chip trade: the S&P 500 rose 1.3% to 7,619.38, Intel jumped 7.5% and Tesla gained 2.9%, while SpaceX slipped ahead of Friday's Starship flight.
points: The S&P 500 rose 98.45 points (1.3%) to 7,619.38, the Nasdaq added 1.6% to 25,466.19 and the Dow gained 0.5% to 52,486.49. Chips did the work: CoreWeave beat on Q3 revenue, raised its 2026 revenue guide to $13.0-13.3 billion and lifted the low end of its capex range to $37-39 billion, and the stock jumped roughly 20-25%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index climbed 5.7% with every member higher: AMD +7.3% to 552.90, Micron +11.9% to 811.30, Intel +7.5%. Apple set a record high after a China Renaissance upgrade to Buy.

Nvidia closed up 2.9% at 173.73, ending a two-day slide, then fell 8 to 9% after hours once the Wall Street Journal reported the board was preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang and the New York Times alleged a second relationship with an executive; Reuters said the board met late into Wednesday night without announcing a decision. That is Thursday's overhang, with earnings due November 17.

Tesla gained 2.9% to 390.84 after Finland approved its FSD driver-assistance system for its roads and Musk said Cybertruck production will be extended. Intel rose 7.5% to 62.50 on about 126 million shares, recovering from the post-midterm chip selloff tied to worries about tighter AI regulation and data-center permitting. SpaceX slipped 2.3% to 139.75 against the up market, with traders cautious ahead of Starship Flight 15 on Friday and a December insider lockup expiry in view.

The Treasury market was closed for Veterans Day, so there was no bond read on Tuesday's hot October CPI (headline +0.4%, core +0.3%, both above forecast). On Tuesday the 10-year yield had climbed about 12 bp to roughly 5% and the 2-year to 4.74%; CME FedWatch now prices about an 85% chance of a quarter-point hike at the December 8-9 meeting and roughly 15% for a half point, after Governor Waller said a half-point move should be considered if core came in at 0.3% or higher. Treasuries reopen Thursday.

pick.name: Micron Technology
pick.theme: Memory maker rebounding from a 25% monthly drawdown as AI capex guidance firms up
pick.what: Micron makes DRAM and NAND memory, including the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) that sits next to AI accelerators in data-center servers. It is one of three major DRAM suppliers worldwide and has been posting record margins as memory prices rise.
pick.why: The stock jumped 11.9% to 811.30 on November 11 after CoreWeave raised its 2026 capex floor to $37-39 billion, which investors read as more demand for DRAM and HBM, and Morgan Stanley said the valuation pullback had improved memory stocks' risk-reward. That bounce follows a roughly 25% slide over the past month, from 983.23 on October 28 to 656.39 on November 5, so the shares still sit about 35% below the June 52-week high of 1,255. TipRanks shows a Strong Buy consensus with 28 Buy ratings out of 29 and an average target near $1,624, while MarketBeat's more conservative tally is Moderate Buy with an average target of about $1,408; even the lower figure is well above the current price. An idea to research, not a recommendation.
pick.risk: Memory is a cyclical commodity business: the same pricing that drives record margins can reverse quickly, and the stock just showed it can lose 17% in a single session. Any pause in AI data-center spending, including the political scrutiny of data-center construction that triggered the November selloff, would hit Micron harder than most chip names. With a December Fed hike now priced in, high-multiple semiconductors are also exposed to rising rates.

btc.summary: In his newest bitcoin video, posted Wednesday morning, Cowen says the weekly close back under the 50-week moving average, after only a short run above it, looks like a bull trap: the reclaim produced roughly a 10% gain, against about 30% after comparable reclaims in 2019 and 2023, so the breakout never had the strength of the ones that started real legs higher. He reads the slide as driven mainly by the correction in stocks rather than anything specific to crypto, and expects it to keep going in stages, with temporary bounces, rather than one clean flush. His base case is still a fourth-quarter low, with December the most likely window, and he points to the Fed's December meeting as a possible turning point if markets start to anticipate the end of rate increases, as they did near the December 2018 low.

brief.lede: Nvidia's board met into the night on whether to remove Jensen Huang, GXO signed for up to 1,000 Apptronik humanoids, Anthropic's IPO is many times oversubscribed, and MSCI is dropping Strategy from its indexes as bitcoin ETF outflows reach a fifth day.

articles.title: GXO signs for up to 1,000 Apptronik Apollo humanoids
body: GXO Logistics and Apptronik said on November 12 that they have signed a letter of intent to move Apollo from pilots toward a fleet of **up to 1,000 humanoid robots over four years**, with the first North American deployment planned for late 2027. The agreement widens trials in live warehouses from 2027 across picking, moving totes and cases, packing and sortation. It is not a purchase order: the companies said the rollout depends on the robots meeting agreed productivity, safety and operational targets.

The two companies began with a proof of concept in 2024, and Apollo completed a US pilot with GXO earlier this year. The commercial model would be robotics-as-a-service, meaning GXO would pay for robot time rather than buy the hardware outright. Forbes noted that GXO is also running Agility's Digit and machines from Reflex Robotics, so the contract logistics company is positioning itself as a shared proving ground rather than committing to one vendor.

The timing helps Apptronik. Two days earlier Google DeepMind used Apollo's **96 percent success rate** on a parts-kitting pilot at Mercedes-Benz as the showcase for its Gemini Robotics 2.5 model, and Agility, GXO's other humanoid supplier, listed on Nasdaq last week with milestone-linked Digit orders. Conditional, staged commitments tied to a named list of tasks are becoming the standard shape of a humanoid deal.

J.P. Morgan put numbers on that ramp the same day. In a report covered by Reuters, the bank projected US humanoid production of **300,000 to 400,000 units by 2030** and about 1.5 million by 2035, arguing that the industry is shifting from demonstrations to commercial deployment. It listed hardware, AI training data, compute and production capacity as the main constraints.

Those forecasts dwarf today's output. The most recent third-party estimate put worldwide shipments at about 16,500 humanoids in the third quarter, led by Chinese makers, and US companies have so far reported builds in the hundreds or low thousands. Getting from there to hundreds of thousands a year means solving actuator supply, battery life and the data pipeline at the same time, which is what the bank's list of constraints points at.

What to watch: whether GXO's 2027 trials disclose the performance thresholds that trigger the 1,000-unit path, and whether Apptronik's late-2027 date holds alongside Agility's first-half 2027 Digit 5 deliveries. For engineers, the practical signal is that warehouse picking and tote handling, not factory kitting alone, is now the task set a humanoid has to prove itself on.

articles.title: Nvidia's board meets through the night on whether to remove Huang
body: Nvidia's board met late on Wednesday to decide whether Jensen Huang keeps his job, and as of early Thursday it had said nothing. **The Wall Street Journal reported on November 11 that directors were preparing to oust the founder and chief executive**, and Reuters, CNBC and CNN confirmed that the board was meeting on his future. CNBC said the session stretched into the evening without an announcement.

The trigger was a second allegation. The New York Times reported that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, 48, the company's vice president of healthcare, a claim neither has confirmed; Nvidia declined to comment and Powell did not respond. That followed Huang's own admission on Sunday, in a message to employees, of an affair with Alice Huang, a data-center executive at a large customer in Southeast Asia, which earlier reporting had tied to a suspected foreign intelligence effort. The board's independent-director committee and outside counsel, announced days ago, are still at work, and the company has said it has no reason to believe secrets were compromised.

Markets did not wait. **Nvidia shares fell more than 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and were down about 8% again premarket on Thursday**, dragging S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures lower. Bernstein cut the stock to market-perform and halved its price target to $200 from $400. AMD and Broadcom rose premarket as investors looked for alternative suppliers, and William Blair upgraded AMD to outperform, citing Nvidia's leadership turmoil and Intel's supply constraints.

There is no obvious successor. Bloomberg reported that the board has been working with an outside search firm, and Semafor said chief financial officer Colette Kress is being considered as an interim chief executive. Under Nvidia's bylaws a majority of directors can remove the CEO with or without cause, which means the decision rests with a small group that has worked alongside Huang for decades.

The timing could hardly be worse. **Nvidia reports third-quarter results on November 17**, with revenue guidance of $108 billion, and the House Select Committee on China has a closed-door briefing on the Huang matter set for November 18. Whatever the board decides, the next six days will test whether the AI hardware trade depends on one person or on a product cycle that runs regardless of who presents it.

articles.title: Anthropic's IPO book is covered many times as bankers eye a bump
body: One day into its roadshow, Anthropic's initial public offering has drawn far more orders than there are shares. **Bloomberg reported on November 11 that the deal is multiple times oversubscribed**, citing people familiar with the matter, with demand driven by anchor-size indications of interest, meaning large investors signaling they want big blocks before the final price is set.

The terms have not changed since Tuesday. Anthropic is marketing 825 million Class A shares at $70 to $78 each, which works out to roughly $64 billion at the top of the range, and has applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT. Including the concurrent private placement to strategic investors, **the company is seeking as much as $90.4 billion**, which would make this the largest IPO on record by a wide margin. TSMC's board has already approved buying up to $500 million of stock at the offer price.

Heavy demand is already feeding talk of a bump. The Financial Times reported that bankers were weighing a price above the current range, according to several outlets summarizing the paper, though no amended filing with a higher range had appeared as of Thursday morning. Several reports put pricing on November 18, which lines up with the trading window flagged earlier this week, but Anthropic has not confirmed a date.

The mood has shifted quickly. As recently as November 6, Bloomberg reported that buyers were discussing a valuation as low as $1.2 trillion to $1.3 trillion, well under the $2 trillion that bankers had floated over the summer. Recent precedent cuts both ways: Cerebras and Figma both raised more than they first indicated as demand built, and both now trade below their offer prices.

The deal is also landing in a jittery market. Nvidia's leadership crisis sent Nasdaq futures lower on Thursday, a reminder that the biggest AI listing ever will price into whatever the chip trade looks like next week. **If underwriters do lift the range, the final number will say more about investor appetite for AI than any benchmark released this month.**

articles.title: MSCI boots Strategy as bitcoin ETF outflows stretch to five days
body: MSCI said on Wednesday, November 11 that it will remove Strategy, the software company turned bitcoin holding vehicle run by Michael Saylor, from its global indexes, including the MSCI USA Index, **effective after the close on November 30**. It is the first deletion under a new rule for companies without substantive operating assets: such issuers must pass five financial ratio screens, and failing four or more costs them index eligibility. Strategy skipped the usual two-year grace period for existing members and went straight onto the deletion list.

The index provider in effect decided that Strategy looks more like a bitcoin fund than an operating business. JPMorgan has estimated roughly $2.8 billion of forced selling by funds that track MSCI, rising to about $8.8 billion if other index providers follow. Japan's Metaplanet and Upexi were flagged for removal as well, and Sharplink was placed on a watchlist, so the rule reaches well beyond one company.

The removal affects the stock, not the coins. Nothing in the index rules forces Strategy to sell bitcoin, and CoinDesk noted that the real risk is to its financing model: the company has funded its purchases by issuing equity and convertible debt into passive demand that will now shrink. Strategy closed at $122.35 on Wednesday, about 11% below the $137.21 of bitcoin backing each share by one outlet's count.

Spot bitcoin ETFs, meanwhile, bled for a **fifth straight session, losing about $299.8 million on November 11**, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for roughly 90% of the day. The streak that began November 5 has now drained about $1.44 billion. Bitcoin traded near $73,400 on Wednesday, down about 0.7% as tech stocks fell, and was quoted around $73,444 early Thursday, about 8.7% lower over the week.

That leaves the price below the roughly $75,600 average cost basis of short-term holders, a level analysts watch because coins held at a loss tend to be sold into rallies. The next catalyst is Friday's producer price report; after Tuesday's hot consumer inflation print, a warm wholesale number would firm up expectations of a December rate increase and keep pressure on risk assets.

What comes next is a test of whether the bitcoin treasury trade can survive without index plumbing. Strategy's premium to its holdings has already flipped to a discount, and if the forced selling in late November is as large as JPMorgan expects, the company's ability to keep buying could stall just as ETF demand has gone quiet.

articles.title: Finland clears Tesla's FSD; Cybertruck gets a summer 2027 reprieve
body: Finland's transport regulator Traficom has recognized the provisional Dutch type approval for Tesla's supervised self-driving software, making it the **11th European country** to allow the system on its roads. The decision is dated November 10 and was reported Wednesday. The feature is sold in Europe as Tesla Assisted Driving after Tesla agreed to changes, including limits on speed settings, and Traficom put the number of eligible cars in Finland at about 6,500.

The agency was careful to call it a driver assistance system and warned that snow, slush and dirt on the cameras can degrade performance, a real concern in a Finnish winter. It also said the national recognition does not bind Finland's vote in the EU-wide process, where a final decision on the software is expected next year. Still, each country that signs on makes that vote easier for Tesla.

Separately, Elon Musk reversed course on the Cybertruck. After saying on November 6 that the Giga Texas line would wind down around mid-2027 to make room for Cybercab, and on November 9 that it would shut in about eight months with deposits refunded, he posted on November 11 that **production will continue through the end of summer 2027** to clear the order backlog. He admitted it was not the best financial decision for Tesla; fans had pushed back hard. Tesla has not issued a formal statement.

Tesla's Semi program had a rare concrete data point: the company confirmed a batch of 50 electric trucks headed to Chicago, where dealer HMD took its first unit on November 2. Electrek noted Tesla still discloses little about Semi output or fleet size. Tesla shares closed at **$390.84 on Wednesday, up 2.9%**, with the Finland approval and the Cybertruck extension cited as drivers.

On the SpaceX side, nothing has changed on paper: Starship Flight 15 is still targeted for Friday, November 13, with the window opening at 2:45 PM Pacific, and as of the latest reports the FAA's Starship page still did not list the license modification that would cover bringing the ship back over populated areas for a tower catch. President Gwynne Shotwell has said she expects it to be granted with both catches included.

The next 36 hours will tell. If the license lands and the weather holds, Friday afternoon could deliver the first ship catch in the program's history; if not, the date slides, as every Starship date is published as no earlier than. Either way, Tesla heads into the weekend with one more regulatory win in Europe and a truck line it was ready to kill a week ago.

articles.title: Senate attaches three China chip bills to the defense bill
body: The Huang affair has given export-control hawks in Congress an opening, and they are using it. **The Senate's fiscal 2027 defense authorization bill now carries three China-focused chip measures**: the Chip Security Act, the AI Overwatch Act and the MATCH Act, Korea Times reported on November 11, with the Senate text still to be reconciled with the House version before anything becomes law.

The AI Overwatch Act, sponsored by Senator Jim Banks, would write limits on exports of top-end AI chips to countries of concern into statute and give Congress a review window over Commerce Department export licenses. It would also require officials to weigh whether a license for less advanced chips could enable remote access by unauthorized parties, the loophole that lets Chinese labs rent Nvidia hardware in third countries without any chip crossing the border.

Banks and Senator Elizabeth Warren issued a joint statement urging passage, pointing to reports that Nvidia has received approvals to ship large volumes of chips to China, including to firms linked to the military. The Daily Caller reported the same day on fresh evidence of Chinese workarounds to existing rules. The reporting about Huang's foreign contacts has made it harder for the company's allies to argue that the current regime is sufficient.

The industry is pushing back through the White House. Politico reported that Nvidia and AMD are urging the administration to lean on Congress to drop or narrow the provisions. **The White House remains the biggest variable**: the president has repeatedly opposed mandatory AI rules, but a defense bill is must-pass legislation and a veto override needs two-thirds of both chambers.

The remote-access question has been stuck for most of the year. The House passed the Remote Access Security Act 369 to 22 in January, and it has sat in the Senate Banking Committee since; Commerce was reported in August to be drafting its own rule on cloud rentals. With the House Select Committee on China briefing on Huang scheduled for November 18, the odds of the NDAA conference keeping at least one of these provisions look better than they did a week ago.

articles.title: Blocking one enzyme in old mice adds four months of median life
body: A drug that inhibits asparagine endopeptidase, a protein-cutting enzyme also known as legumain or delta-secretase, extended the lives of mice when treatment began at 18 months, roughly the equivalent of late middle age. In a study published in iScience by Yang and colleagues, animals fed a diet containing the inhibitor, called compound 11a, saw **median survival rise from 24 to 28 months, a gain of about 17%**. The effect held in both sexes, although females lived shorter lives than males in both the treated and control groups.

The survival gain came with better function. The authors report that treated mice scored lower on multiple frailty indices and showed slower age-related decline in physical and cognitive tests. Fight Aging, which highlighted the paper on Wednesday, pointed out that a 17% late-life extension is in the same range as rapamycin started in old mice, which remains the benchmark for drug interventions begun late.

The enzyme is not an obscure target. Asparagine endopeptidase has been studied for years in Alzheimer's models, where it cleaves tau and amyloid precursor protein into fragments that drive pathology, and the same inhibitor family has been tested in senescence-accelerated mice. What is new is treating ordinary aged animals and measuring lifespan rather than a single disease readout. The authors themselves caution that the mechanistic evidence in naturally aged mice remains largely correlative.

A second item from the same source takes a stranger route to candidate drugs. On Tuesday, Fight Aging covered a study that mined long-term rodent toxicology trials, the kind run on pesticides for regulatory approval, for signs of hormesis, the idea that a mild stress can trigger a protective response. **Of 154 substances, 27 significantly increased survival** at study termination, about 18% of the entries. One of them, the herbicide bromoxynil, was then tested in nematode worms, where it improved several healthspan measures without obvious harm.

Nobody is suggesting people take weed killer. The value of the toxicology approach is that it reuses decades of expensive, well-controlled rodent survival data that were collected for a different purpose, and survival at termination is a crude endpoint that other factors can move. Still, it is a cheap way to generate a list of molecules that someone can then test properly.

The asparagine endopeptidase result is the one to watch. The compound is orally available, the effect size is competitive, and the target has a clinical rationale from neurodegeneration. The usual caveats apply: it is one lab, one strain, and the leap from mouse median survival to human healthspan has broken many promising molecules. An independent replication, ideally through the NIA's Interventions Testing Program, would be the natural next step.

vocab.def: Casually unconcerned; carefree in a way that shows a light, almost careless lack of worry.

cards.b: French insouciant, from in- ('not') and soucier ('to care'), from Latin sollicitare ('to disturb')
nonchalant, carefree, breezy, unbothered
a surfer shrugging at a wipeout, a founder joking through a bad quarter, a cat on a warm car hood

examples: He gave an insouciant shrug when the demo robot fell over, and the room relaxed with him.
There's an insouciant charm to a city that closes its best street for a Sunday market.
vocab.ex: He gave an insouciant shrug when the demo robot fell over, and the room relaxed with him.

vocab.def: The tendency to see meaningful patterns or connections in random or unrelated data.

cards.b: Coined by German psychiatrist Klaus Conrad in 1958, from Greek apo- ('away from') and phainein ('to show')
patternicity, false pattern, seeing faces in clouds
a backtest that only looks predictive, a 'trend' in three data points, a conspiracy theory

examples: Three green days in a row isn't a signal; that's apophenia talking.
Robot logs invite apophenia: every glitch looks like a pattern until you count.
vocab.ex: Three green days in a row isn't a signal; that's apophenia talking.

vocab.def: Calm self-confidence, especially in a tense or difficult situation.

cards.b: French 'à plomb', 'according to the plumb line', meaning upright and steady
poise, composure, assurance
handling pressure gracefully: a demo gone wrong, a hard question, a surprise

examples: She fielded the hostile question with perfect aplomb.
The robot demo failed, but he recovered with aplomb.
vocab.ex: She fielded the hostile question with perfect aplomb.

vocab.def: Impossible to avoid or escape; certain to happen no matter what you do.

cards.b: Latin 'ineluctabilis', from in- (not) + eluctari (to struggle out of)
inescapable, unavoidable, inevitable
fate, deadlines, or facts that no amount of effort changes

examples: The ineluctable arrival of winter sent everyone indoors.
He felt the ineluctable pull of the old neighborhood.
vocab.ex: The ineluctable arrival of winter sent everyone indoors.

vocab.def: A very fine, light, delicate material, like spider silk; or anything that feels that thin and airy.

cards.b: Middle English; often traced to 'goose summer', the warm autumn days when floating spider silk is seen
filmy, sheer, diaphanous
cobwebs in morning light, thin fabric, or something fragile and barely there

examples: Gossamer threads of spider silk caught the low autumn sun.
She wore a gossamer scarf that moved with every breath of wind.
vocab.ex: Gossamer threads of spider silk caught the low autumn sun.

vocab.def: Relating to twilight; describing animals that are most active at dawn and dusk.

cards.b: From Latin crepusculum, 'twilight'
dusky, dim, twilit
animals like rabbits, deer and owls that move around at dawn and dusk, or any soft low light

examples: The crepuscular glow made the whole street look gold.
Rabbits are crepuscular, so the best time to spot them is just after sunrise.
vocab.ex: The crepuscular glow made the whole street look gold.

cards.b: From Latin pellucidus, from per-, 'through', and lucidus, 'shining'
limpid, transparent, lucid
water or glass you can see through, and writing or explanations that are crystal clear

examples: The pond was so pellucid he could count the stones on the bottom.
Her pellucid explanation made the whole contract make sense.
vocab.ex: The pond was so pellucid he could count the stones on the bottom.

spanish.note: Literally 'what a bear', but in Mexico it's the everyday way to say 'how embarrassing' or 'how awkward', about yourself or someone else. 'Hacer el oso' is to embarrass yourself in public.

cards.en: I'm embarrassed / it makes me shy

parts.en: to make a fool of yourself

dialog.es: Le dije 'mamá' a la maestra enfrente de todos.
dialog.en: I called the teacher 'mom' in front of everyone.
How embarrassing! And what did you do?

dialog.es: Nada, me puse rojo y me senté.
dialog.en: Nothing, I turned red and sat down.

dialog.es: Ya ni modo, mañana nadie se acuerda.
dialog.en: Oh well, tomorrow nobody will remember.

spanish.use: Say it with a wince when someone trips, waves at the wrong person or replies-all by mistake.

spanish.note: Literally 'to little', but in Mexico it's the everyday way to say 'really?' or 'you're kidding' when something surprises you. Flip it to '¿a poco no?' and it means 'right?' or 'isn't it?'

cards.en: No way! / Don't make it up!

dialog.en: They offered me a job in Guadalajara.
Really? That's great!
Yes, I start in January.
Well, congratulations, we have to celebrate.

spanish.use: Say it with raised eyebrows the moment someone surprises you.

spanish.note: Literally 'it's of hairs', but in Mexican slang 'de pelos' means excellent or really good. Use it for food, plans, music, anything you like.

dialog.en: Did you try the new tacos?
Yes, they're awesome!
Shall we go again tomorrow?
Deal, we'll go tomorrow.

spanish.use: Say it when something is better than you expected.

spanish.meaning: I can't be bothered to go out
spanish.note: 'Flojera' is laziness, but in Mexican Spanish 'me da flojera' is a relaxed way to say you don't feel like doing something. It isn't a harsh judgment of yourself. Swap in any verb: 'me da flojera cocinar'.

dialog.en: Shall we go to the movies tonight?
Ugh, I can't be bothered to go out.

dialog.es: Pedimos pizza y vemos algo en casa.
dialog.en: We'll order pizza and watch something at home.
Now that's a great idea!

spanish.use: Say it when a plan sounds fine but your couch sounds better.

options: I can't be bothered to go out

spanish.meaning: I like your friend (he's easy to get along with)
spanish.note: In Mexican Spanish 'caer bien' means that someone strikes you as likeable. It's about the person's vibe, not romance. The opposite is 'caer mal' or, more bluntly, 'caer gordo'.

dialog.en: What did you think of Luis?

dialog.es: Me cae bien tu amigo, es muy relajado.
dialog.en: I like your friend, he's very laid back.
Yeah, he always makes me laugh.

dialog.es: Invítalo otra vez, me cae bien.
dialog.en: Invite him again, I like him.

spanish.use: Say it after meeting someone you got along with, to tell a friend your first impression.

spanish.note: In Mexican Spanish, 'ya estuvo' closes something off. It can mean 'that's done', 'we're all set', or, with the right tone, 'that's enough'. Context and your voice do the work.

dialog.en: Do you still need anything from the store?
No, that's everything, thanks.
Sure? There's still time.
Yes, we're done. Let's go.

spanish.use: Say it when a task is finished, an order is complete, or you want to politely end something.

spanish.note: In Mexican Spanish, 'al rato' means 'in a while' or 'later', usually the same day. It's a loose way to say goodbye when you expect to see someone again soon.

dialog.en: I'm going to eat, shall we meet later?
Sure. What time do you finish?
Around four.
Perfect, see you in a bit.

spanish.use: Say it when you're parting ways and expect to meet again the same day.

Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos

dare.title: Find out your mile time
dare.why: Sunny by noon and 74, so take a lunch hour or the last light before sunset at 4:59 PM. Warm up ten minutes, then run one measured mile as hard as you can hold, on the flat Stevens Creek Trail with your watch for distance, or four laps of any 400-meter track. No music, and write the number down somewhere you'll find it in six months.
dare.worth: A mile time is one honest number that tells you more about your fitness than any step count, and once you have one you'll want to beat it. Most people haven't run an all-out mile since school and are surprised by how alive the last lap feels.

swap.title: Learn the NATO alphabet by heart
swap.why: Alfa through Zulu, 26 words. Say them out loud in groups of five, then spell your name, your street and your license plate with them. Test yourself once more before bed.
swap.worth: You'll use it on every bad phone line and support call for the rest of your life, and it takes one evening.
